fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Night-time conspicuity of a HAWK display against competing background elements is a substantive safety issue at an arterial pedestrian crossing, directly relevant to a final-design-stage audit.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (driver confusion from competing night-time background elements at this site) is supported by a verbatim quote in EV-US-001 tied to the FHWA case study Table A.10 Issue 6, exceeding registry-citation-only cap.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern under FHWA RSA semantics with no compliance/MUTCD conflation, and the driver-confusion-to-pedestrian-risk link is transparently labelled as inference.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Reflective border installation is specific to the named intersection, actionable at final design stage, and a recognized viable conspicuity countermeasure for signal heads.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are explicitly identified as the exposed users if drivers misread or detect the beacon late, pairing driver conspicuity with VRU protection where it is directly applicable.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance adequacy for slower walkers at the corridor's highest collision-frequency HAWK sites is a substantive final-design-stage VRU safety issue affecting real exposure.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim is directly supported by the verbatim EV-US-016 quote ('The pedestrian clearance interval may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians'), exceeding registry-id-only citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern distinct from any compliance question, consistent with FHWA RSA semantics for signal timing review at final design.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Reprogramming clearance intervals at all six named sites using a reduced assumed walking speed is specific, actionable, and standard viable signal-retiming practice.
justifications.vru_coverage: Elderly pedestrians are explicitly identified as affected road users and the entire finding centers on their crossing exposure, fully addressing VRU impact.
